newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies expected higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies expected higher.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open 0.200 to 0.300 cent per lb higher while pork bellies were called 0.500 to 1.000 cent higher, livestock analysts said.

Hog futures were expected to resume their upward trend after spillover pressure from live cattle futures late Wednesday. Further strength in cash hog markets on strong packer demand should lift futures prices early, they said.

Hog numbers are seen tightening seasonally with farmer fieldwork adding to the short supply. Continued expectations of increased demand for U.S. pork due to the Taiwan pork ban should also lend support, they said.

Demand for U.S. pork has already started to increase in the wake of Taiwan's pork export ban, as Japan trade houses confirmed reports that they are buying U.S. pork bellies. They told Reuters they will be buying U.S. bellies until late May to fill needs into the end of the year.

Traders said the Japan buying should spark further demand for pork belly futures, especially with futures closing technically strong after reaching eight-month highs and cash bellies at highest price levels since early October. Belly storings reportedly ran light during early April, they added.
